accuracy.evidence: Checked against the topic's evidence statements (describe how an action affected someone, predict before acting, explain after a conflict what could have been done differently), CASEL's SEL framework (self-awareness, social awareness, and responsible decision-making including anticipating and evaluating the consequences of one's actions), the DfE (2019) statutory Relationships Education guidance (caring friendships; respectful relationships, including the conventions of courtesy and the steps children can take to improve relationships) and the PSHE Association KS2 programme of study. Intent and impact are defined consistently, cues are limited to observable face, body, words and actions, and the lesson does not tell children that intent is irrelevant, only that it does not cancel the impact.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common errors named in SEL practice: judging by intent only ('Yes, if I meant it kindly' prediction, 'I was only joking' as a wrong reply in m4 and the challenge, 'intent' tag, m9), reading your own feelings as theirs ('You were laughing, so it was fine' clue card, m2), irrelevant details as clues (red coat, blue pen, Gran lives far away), telling someone how they feel ('You're fine, right?' card, p3, 'tell' tag), blaming the hurt person ('You're too sensitive', 'Don't be a bad loser', 'blame' tag) and acting on impulse (grab cards, 'grab' tag).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagimpact is built around an impact meter: a five-face track with a draggable dot that shows how an action lands for the other person. The child sets the dot from a clue, then every choice card dropped in the box moves the dot live, so a wrong choice is felt on the meter before the feedback, and Rewind starts the dot low and lifts it with a better move. Shingle similarity is 11.2% with flag_sva.js, 9.7% with flag_blend.js and 7.4% with flag_sorry.js; no other lab uses a meter or intent/impact cards, including Saying sorry (repair steps) and Seeing someone else's point of view.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the gap by doing: the intent bubble ('You meant: it looked funny') sits above a clue that says otherwise, so the dot must go to upset; in Sam's case the two match, showing intent and impact can agree. Testing choices on the meter makes prediction concrete, Rewind shows the same story ending differently, and Check in shows that asking is better than telling. Done lines restate the rule and quote the child's prediction.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the next task tests: 'Yes, if I meant it kindly' (Leo and Ana show a kind or funny intent landing badly), 'Fine: it is only a cookie' (the meter drops to upset when Grab is tried), and 'No, so there was no harm' for Kai (the story starts on upset even though you did not mean it). A.reveal quotes the child's own pick in each done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers; why() names the slip for each: intent ('What you meant matters, but they feel the impact'), joke ('A joke is only funny if the person it is about laughs too'), clue ('Look for real clues: faces, bodies, words and actions'), grab ('Stop and predict'), blame ('Blaming them skips your part') and tell ('Do not tell people how they feel. Ask, then listen'). Every wrong card in the lab also moves the meter and explains itself.

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK 2.6 in short concrete sentences with examples (laughing when a friend trips). Adult text measures FK 6.3 and uses the precise terms intent, impact, consequence, perspective, empathy, cues (facial expression, body language, tone of voice), predict, reflect and check in, with the CASEL, DfE 2019 and PSHE Association references.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed; the largest 6-word-shingle overlap with any other lesson is 0.2%. Kid paragraphs cover the two sides, reading clues, not using your own feelings as the clue, and stop, predict, check in; adult paragraphs give the framework placement, key terms and the three-part skill, five named mistakes with a family routine, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for every step: the You and other-person pictures, the wrapped story, the drop box, the meter with five faces and the current label, and three full-width choice cards (42 px) all fit without overlap; the meter dot is 26 px with a 34 px grab band, and the button twins below wrap cleanly.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five Show me tasks completed, the challenge appeared, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme and there were no console errors. A manual probe dragged the meter dot to upset for Leo and very upset for Ana, then dragged Grab (meter fell, unfair feedback) and Split (very happy) into the box. Every drag has a button twin (five face buttons, one button per card) and the canvas aria-label is updated with every message.
